summary: The note covers the history of Sony Music Entertainment, from its founding as American Record Corporation in 1929 through its acquisition by CBS, the CBS Records era, Sony's 1987-88 purchase, and the 2004 Sony BMG merger and 2008 buyout. It also details label launches, leadership changes (Wallerstein, Conkling, Lieberson, Morris, Reid) and the 2011 restructuring. SME is described as the world's second largest recorded music company, after Universal Music Group.
one_line: History of Sony Music Entertainment from American Record Corporation (1929) through CBS Records, Sony's acquisition, the Sony BMG merger and the 2011 restructuring under Doug Morris.
key_facts: Sony Music Entertainment Inc. (SME) is an American music corporation managed by Sony Corporation of America (SCA), a subsidiary of Japanese conglomerate Sony Corporation, and is the world's second largest recorded music company after Universal Music Group.
The enterprise was founded in 1929 as American Record Corporation (ARC) and renamed Columbia Recording Corporation in 1938 after CBS acquired it; it became CBS Records in 1966.

Ted Wallerstein, an RCA Victor executive, convinced CBS head William S. Paley to buy ARC, and Paley made him head of the company; he spearheaded the introduction of the long playing (LP) record before retiring as chairman in 1951.

Columbia founded Epic Records in 1953 and Date Records in 1958, which initially issued rockabilly; Date's biggest hit was "Time of the Season" by the Zombies, peaking at #2 in 1969, and the label was discontinued in 1970.
In 1986 CBS sold its music publishing arm, CBS Songs, to Stephen Swid, Martin Bandier and Charles Koppelman for $125 million, forming the foundation of SBK Entertainment.

Sony Corporation of Japan bought the company in 1987 and renamed it Sony Music Entertainment on January 1, 1991, as required by the 1988 buyout terms granting only a transitional license to the CBS trademark.
Sony reintroduced the Columbia label worldwide in 1991 after acquiring the international trademark rights from EMI in 1990; Japan is the exception, where Nippon Columbia controls the name.
In 1964 CBS acquired Oriole Records to set up its own UK distribution, and took over distribution from EMI in 1968 when that deal expired.
In 2004 SME and Bertelsmann Music Group merged as Sony BMG; Sony completed its acquisition of Bertelsmann's 50% stake on October 1, 2008, and BMG relaunched as BMG Rights Management.
Doug Morris became chairman and CEO on July 1, 2011; L.A. Reid became chairman and CEO of Epic Records and Peter Edge became CEO of RCA Records.
The RCA Music Group closed Arista, J Records and Jive Records in October 2011, moving their artists to RCA Records.
Barry Weiss, RCA/Jive Label Group CEO since 2008 and head of Jive Records since 1991, left in March 2011 to lead Island Def Jam and Universal Republic.
Mel Lewinter was named Executive Vice President of Label Strategy on October 11, 2011, and Dennis Kooker became President of Global Digital Business and US Sales in January 2012.
Among the Big Three record companies, SME is middle-sized, with Universal Music Group the largest and Warner Music Group the smallest.
